newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU 1997 compound feed output broadly steady - FEFAC.
newsitem.headline: EU 1997 compound feed output broadly steady - FEFAC.

text.p: European compound feed production in 1997 may be one percent below or above the 123 million tonnes seen last year, said Alexander Doehring, secretary general of the EU feed industry lobby FEFAC.
"It's impossible to be more precise at this stage, France believes it will continue at the same pace and Germany may also have another good year," he told the Lipidex 97 oilseeds conference.
France, at 23 million tonnes, was the leading EU producer in 1996, followed by Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Italy and Britain.
Doehring said potentially negative effects from the mad cow disease crisis, which reduced demand for beef feed, were offset by increased demand for broiler and pig feedstuffs.
Potential annual EU cereals use from industrial feed mixers on the basis of current livestock data had been limited at 60 million tonnes in a recent Dreyfus study.
But FEFAC capped possible industrial grains use at 46 million tonnes -- otherwise grain inclusion rates would exceed 50 percent.
The bulk of grains use in feeds is consumed directly on the farm where consumption is difficult to measure.
FEFAC was supportive of EU attempts to encourage subsidy-free meat and dairy exports because expansion in the domestic market did not look possible, Doehring said.
This process should start soon as future world trade rules would necessarily bring limits on such exports.
EU cereals support prices needed to be cut further as feedstuffs were still the single largest cost factor for the livestock industry.

FEFAC was opposed to a link between income support payments to farmers in future EU reforms and extensive farming methods as this was contrary to attempts to achieve the lowest possible production cost.
